stories.title: Harper College launches AI pre-apprenticeship program
stories.summary: Harper College is launching a four-session online AI Pre-apprenticeship in December. The program introduces participants to workplace applications and career pathways in the field. Supported by an Illinois state grant, the initiative targets younger students and working professionals seeking to understand how AI might shape their future careers.

stories.title: Universities face pressure to update career support
stories.summary: Higher education institutions are struggling to keep internal processes aligned with a rapidly shifting labor market. Experts suggest that leaders must move beyond having all the answers, instead prioritizing active listening to business needs and translating that feedback into concrete action to better prepare students for modern employment.

stories.title: Fintech career paths and salary expectations
stories.summary: Working in fintech involves applying technical skills to financial systems and digital payments. According to Singapore’s National Youth Council, software engineers in the sector can earn between S$6,000 and S$9,300 per month. Students and parents are encouraged to evaluate how specific academic programs connect their teaching to industry requirements.

stories.title: L’Oreal seeks advocacy manager for professional products
stories.summary: L’Oreal is recruiting an Advocacy Manager for its Professional Products Division in London. The role involves translating global consumer strategies into local influencer and creator-marketing plans. Candidates are expected to have experience in social media, PR, and brand storytelling to drive digital engagement and campaign execution for the company.

stories.summary: The U.S. Senate Employment Office has opened its 2026 Senators-Elect Resume Collection. This centralized recruitment initiative allows job seekers to be considered for roles in the offices of newly elected senators taking office in January 2027. It serves as a primary gateway for public servants and recent graduates.

stories.title: Student ambassadors weigh in on success initiatives
stories.summary: Four student ambassadors recently addressed the Student Success US conference in Salt Lake City to share their perspectives on higher education. The event, a collaboration between Inside Higher Ed and Times Higher Education, aimed to ensure student voices were represented in discussions regarding how colleges support their academic progress.

stories.title: Cybersecurity certification does not guarantee entry-level roles
stories.summary: Despite earning an Offensive Security Certified Professional certification, some students are finding that advanced qualifications do not necessarily lead to employment. stories.title: Bacon Wilson adds associate attorney to corporate team
stories.summary: Bacon Wilson, P.C. has appointed Emily Oliver as an associate attorney in its Corporate and Commercial Law department. Oliver, who previously served as a law clerk at the firm, was admitted to the Massachusetts Bar on November 17. The firm describes the move as a commitment to emerging talent.

stories.title: Microsoft academy offers datacenter training pathways
stories.summary: The Microsoft Datacenter Academy provides free IT training, mentorship, and hands-on experience in cloud computing and hardware infrastructure. Through partnerships with local colleges and education providers, the program aims to help students and aspiring professionals develop technical skills and explore career opportunities within the growing datacenter industry.

stories.summary: The International Schools Sports Organisation concluded its 2026 National Games Yoga Championship at Symbiosis World School in Pune. The event featured students competing in traditional, artistic, and rhythmic yoga categories. Top performers from the U-14, U-17, and U-19 divisions will now advance to the SGFI National School Games.

stories.summary: The Beacon School for Learners with Special Educational Needs has advanced to the national stage of the World Robot Olympiad. The school, which serves students with autism and severe intellectual disabilities, placed in the top two during provincial rounds to secure its spot in the national coding tournament.

stories.summary: Mirela Grati has been awarded a government scholarship for the 2026 to 2027 academic year. Her career path was reportedly influenced by a volunteer event where she met a medical student.

stories.title: Connect Wayne honors community leaders at gala
stories.summary: Connect Wayne held its inaugural Noche de Gala Awards Ceremony on November 19 in Dudley, North Carolina. The event recognized seven individuals and one business for contributions to the local community across categories including education, entrepreneurship, and advocacy. stories.summary: Super 30 founder Anand Kumar received the Special Achievement Award from Japan’s CGC Group on November 25. The award recognizes his contribution to education and his efforts to provide free, high-quality instruction to economically disadvantaged students. stories.summary: The University of Southampton's Iridis 7 supercomputer has reached 53rd place on the Green500 list, making it the UK's most energy-efficient university-funded system. stories.summary: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk is currently aboard the International Space Station as part of Expedition 75. His wife, Heather Kutryk, gave birth to a daughter on Tuesday. The Canadian Space Agency announced the event, noting the couple considers the birth a blessing.

stories.title: Sustainability rankings show U.S. competitive standing
stories.summary: University Business reports that U.S. institutions remain competitive in sustainability rankings, though the sector continues to face persistent weaknesses. The publication provides research-based approaches for higher education leaders to improve institutional performance and student success.

stories.title: University of Cape Town seeks support for QS rankings
stories.summary: The University of Cape Town is asking researchers to nominate academic peers and employers for the QS World University Rankings reputation survey. The university notes that while rankings help with recruitment and funding, they remain a subject of significant debate within the academic community.

stories.title: Tennessee professor fired over restroom use
stories.summary: The University of Tennessee at Martin has fired an assistant professor for using a staff-only women's restroom. The termination followed a complaint and a written warning citing the Riley Gaines Women's Safety and Protection Act, a state law requiring restroom use to correspond with sex assigned at birth.

stories.title: Naval Academy professor sues over tenure policy
stories.summary: A professor has sued the Department of the Navy after the Secretary of Defense prohibited civilians from being considered for tenure. The directive claims civilian norms dilute the focus on military lethality. The plaintiff, currently on the tenure track, was expecting a review in 2027.

stories.title: Mott Community College removes president
stories.summary: The Board of Trustees at Mott Community College has voted to terminate the contract of President Shaunda Richardson-Snell without cause. The decision followed a two-and-a-half-year tenure and was made during a meeting held largely behind closed doors. The board provided no explanation for the removal.

stories.title: Writers form splinter group amid PEN America tensions
stories.summary: More than 100 writers and artists have formed a new group, PEN Writes US, citing dissatisfaction with PEN America's response to the war in Gaza. The group says it will focus on defending free expression and supporting writers, following three years of internal tension at the organization.

research.title: Typical-query energy figures mislead institutional AI electricity demand
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Institutions increasingly buy large language model services, yet we still often estimate electricity use as single Wh-per-query value. We present the Surrogate Large Language Energy Emulator (SULLEE), an open bottom-up model linking token geometry, serving hardware. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: In some educational institutions, workflows such as the exam deferral process can be slow, inconvenient, and inconsistent, which creates the need to implement novel digital systems. This paper presents Schedulater, a mobile app for managing university. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: New nose drops restore youthful memory and fight Alzheimer’s in aging mice
research.summary: A revolutionary new nasal treatment has restored youthful learning and memory performance in aging mice while preventing severe cognitive decline in mice with Alzheimer’s-like disease. Developed using technology similar to COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, the nose drops stimulate production of a brain-protecting protein that strengthens neurons and supports memory.
